clue.text: Reportedly recognises a bellows-mender's instrument

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word for recognises is taken by its sound alone

parts.note: to recognise something is to know it
Francis Flute is the bellows-mender in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: Someone apparently identifies the musical instrument belonging to a man who repairs bellows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' turns KNOWS into its sound-alike NOSE. The bellows-mender is Flute, one of the amateur actors in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a flute blown through the nostrils, played in Polynesia and elsewhere, so it is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Fellow going over old city in Belgian province

indicators.note: going over means turning back, so the word for fellow is read backwards

parts.note: a fellow is a man
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A man travels across an ancient city into a Belgian region.
explanation.definitionFit: Namur is a province of Wallonia in southern Belgium, named after its capital.

clue.text: Skit involving Liberal makes us cross

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the satire wraps round the abbreviation

parts.note: a skit is a short satire

explanation.surface: A comic sketch about the Liberal party annoys us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' reads as angry but is the noun: the saltire, St Andrew's cross, is part of the Union flag, hence 'makes us'.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltire is a diagonal cross shaped like an X, as on the Scottish flag.

clue.text: Female oddly losing head with violent passion

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the word for oddly is dropped

parts.note: oddly means curiously, strangely

explanation.surface: A woman, behaving strangely, loses her temper in a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like an alternate-letter signal, but here it is the synonym CURIOUSLY, which loses its C.
explanation.definitionFit: Furiously means with rage or fierce intensity, so in violent passion.

clue.text: Like coffee hastily prepared in tube?

definitions.meaning: beans rushed through the grinder would be ground too little
the tube is the London ... railway

explanation.definitionFit: Read as under-ground it means insufficiently ground, like rushed coffee; the tube is the London Underground railway.

clue.text: Cockney toerag, a slippery type

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker of London traditionally drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: a heel is a contemptible person, like a toerag

explanation.surface: A London rogue is called a shifty sort.
explanation.walkthrough: A toerag is British slang for a worthless person; Cockneys, East Londoners, drop their aitches, so HEEL loses H.
explanation.definitionFit: An eel is a slippery fish, and figuratively an evasive person.

clue.text: Heap of potatoes left in holiday accommodation

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for left is placed inside the word for holiday accommodation

parts.note: a camp, such as a holiday camp, provides holiday accommodation

explanation.surface: A pile of spuds has been abandoned at a holiday camp.
explanation.definitionFit: In farming, a clamp is a heap of root crops such as potatoes stored under straw and earth for winter.

clue.text: Jazz group let out initially from Sri Lankan port

indicators.note: from here means taken away from, so letters are removed from the port's name

parts.note: Colombo is the chief port of Sri Lanka

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words let and out

explanation.surface: A band is released, to start with, from a harbour city in Sri Lanka.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes L and O from 'let out', which come out of COLOMBO.
explanation.definitionFit: A combo is a small jazz or dance band.

clue.text: Fine condiment originally taken with a sheep's tongue

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
A1 means first-rate, fine, with the 1 written as the letter I

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of condiment

explanation.surface: A good sauce first served with sheep's tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade runs A RAM + AI + C, so the pieces come in a different order from the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramaic is an ancient Semitic language, and a tongue is a language.

clue.text: Feed person who demonstrates without purpose

indicators.note: without means outside here, so the demonstrator surrounds the word for purpose

parts.note: a prover is one who proves, demonstrates
an end is a purpose or aim

explanation.surface: A protester is fed though he marches aimlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside, as in the old hymn 'a green hill far away, without a city wall'.
explanation.definitionFit: Provender is animal fodder, food or feed.

clue.text: Gentle, blushing girl

parts.note: gentle means mild
a blushing face is red

explanation.surface: A shy, mild-mannered girl turns pink.
explanation.definitionFit: Mildred is a girl's given name, so a girl is a fair crossword definition for it.

clue.text: It's a pain if pup finally slips lead!

indicators.note: slips means lets go of, so a letter drops out of the word for lead

parts.note: plumbago is an old name for graphite, the black lead of pencils

indicators.note: finally points to the final letter of the word pup

explanation.surface: A dog-walker's back gives way when the puppy suddenly pulls free of its lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a dog's leash but is the metal-like graphite, PLUMBAGO; 'finally' picks P, the last letter of pup, and 'slips' drops it to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is pain in the lower back, so it is fairly described as a pain.

clue.text: Thick-skinned type making money

definitions.meaning: an animal with a famously thick hide, the rhinoceros, in short form
an old British slang word for cash

explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is short for rhinoceros, a thick-skinned beast, and also old British slang for money.

clue.text: Discount expert intervening he's a scoundrel

indicators.note: intervening means coming between, so the word for expert goes inside the word for discount

parts.note: a rebate is a discount or partial refund
a pro is a professional, an expert

explanation.surface: A shady man of business who interferes with discounts is condemned as a villain.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is an unprincipled person, a synonym for a scoundrel.

clue.text: Irritable couple talked of cactus

parts.note: a prickly person is touchy, irritable

indicators.note: talked of means spoken, so the word for couple is replaced by its sound-alike

parts.note: a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: Two short-tempered people discuss a spiny plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The prickly pear is an opuntia, a cactus with edible fruit.

clue.text: Regularly pursued employment

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the following word, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Someone who kept up steady work.
explanation.definitionFit: Use means employment in the sense of putting something to work, as in the employment of force.

clue.text: Provide furnishings before magistrate takes case

parts.note: to be up before a magistrate is to appear in court
a holster is a case for a pistol

explanation.surface: Someone supplies furniture before a magistrate takes on his case.
explanation.definitionFit: To upholster is to fit chairs and sofas with padding and covers, providing soft furnishings.

clue.text: Puritanical artist unexpectedly fortified with spirits

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the letters of artist turn up in a surprising new order

parts.note: a drink laced with spirits has had alcohol added

explanation.surface: A prudish painter has, against expectations, had his drink spiked with alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Strait-laced means prudish and strict in morals, like the Puritans.

clue.text: Feudal superior told untruths about supporter rising with soldiers

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for told untruths surrounds the rest

parts.note: lied means told untruths

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a leg supports a table or a body
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A nobleman lied about a supporter who rose with an army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reads upwards in a down clue, so the supporter comes out backwards; 'about' wraps the lying word round it and the soldiers. OR (other ranks) is the usual crossword shorthand for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege lord is a feudal overlord to whom vassals owe allegiance.

clue.text: Fats's bloomer introducing Rose? One's lucky he broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored and the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Fats Waller is asked about his flower song, and the man is said to be a lucky one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges ONESLUCKYHE. Honeysuckle Rose is a 1929 song by the jazz pianist Fats Waller, so the flower comes before Rose in his title.
explanation.definitionFit: The song title is Honeysuckle Rose, and honeysuckle is a flowering plant, a bloomer.

clue.text: Put hours in observing what House of Peers did particularly well?

definitions.text: what House of Peers did particularly well

indicators.note: put in tells us the abbreviation for hours goes inside the word for observing

parts.note: noting means observing

explanation.surface: Someone puts in hours watching what the Lords excelled at.
explanation.walkthrough: In Gilbert and Sullivan's Iolanthe, the House of Peers 'did nothing in particular, and did it very well'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iolanthe song says the Lords did nothing in particular and did it very well, a joke on idleness.

clue.text: Capital is squandered getting average degree

indicators.note: squandered means thrown away, so the word is is lost from the capital

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France

explanation.surface: A spendthrift wastes capital but still emerges with a middling result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' sounds financial but is the city PARIS, which loses IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the normal or average standard or level, as in feeling below par.

clue.text: Agent upset Welsh girl's cat

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a rep, a sales representative, is an agent
Sian is a Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: A salesman trips over a Welsh woman's pet cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The Persian is a long-haired breed of domestic cat.

clue.text: Modern lady excited about novel treat

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one rearrangement is wrapped round the other
excited suggests the letters of lady are stirred up into a new order
novel means new, so the letters of treat are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A fashionable woman gets thrilled by an unusual delicacy.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagrams nest: 'excited' scrambles the lady into the outer letters L-DAY, and 'novel' scrambles the treat into the middle; 'about' signals the wrapping. 'Modern' is the definition, not part of the surface's lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Latter-day means of recent times, contemporary, so it is a synonym for modern.

clue.text: One of two writers needing material brought up

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means lifted so the word reads from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: toile is a linen or cotton fabric

explanation.surface: A pair of authors need some cloth fetched.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot and T S Eliot are two famous writers sharing the surname.

clue.text: Bird biting off top of rue

indicators.note: biting off the top removes the first letter of the word for rue

parts.note: to rue something is to regret it

explanation.surface: A bird nibbles the tip of a herb called rue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rue' looks like the herb but is the verb meaning REGRET.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white heron, a wading bird.

clue.text: Curry favour, writing play about a duke

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for play goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to toy is to play

explanation.surface: A playwright flatters the nobility by writing a drama about a duke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writing' is a joining word in the surface; 'play' is the verb TOY, not a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: To toady is to fawn or flatter servilely, to curry favour.

clue.text: Attempt to close popular Italian college

indicators.note: to close means to enclose, so the word for attempt shuts round the other pieces

parts.note: a try is an attempt
in means popular, fashionable
It is short for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: An effort is made to shut down a well-liked Italian college.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinity is the name of colleges at Cambridge, Oxford and Dublin.

clue.text: The old Syrian leader? That's 27

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the, as in Ye Olde Shoppe

indicators.note: leader points to the first letter of Syrian

explanation.surface: Was this the former ruler of Syria?
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is RIGHT, so the definition reads 'That's right', an affirmative.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'that's right' is an agreeing affirmative, the same as the word of assent.

clue.text: Foreign objects formerly relating to the ear area

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
otic is the anatomical adjective for things of the ear

explanation.surface: A doctor finds things from abroad in a patient's ear that once belonged elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotica are curious objects from foreign lands, things that are exotic.

clue.text: It's what you deserve when it serves you this

definitions.text: It's what you deserve when it serves you this

parts.words: It's what you deserve when it serves you this
parts.note: the idiom 'it serves you ___' means you got what you deserved; the missing word completes it

explanation.definitionFit: Serves you right is said when someone gets their just deserts, and right also means what one is due.

clue.text: Harshness of jazz style common at first in city

parts.note: stride is a jazz piano style with a leaping left hand

indicators.note: in places the first letter of common inside the city abbreviation

parts.note: NY is short for New York City

indicators.note: at first points to the first letter of common

explanation.surface: A loud jazz band's grating sound was common at first in the big city.
explanation.definitionFit: Stridency is shrill harshness of sound or manner.
